html:
The Saxons were a Germanic people of northern Germany, between the Elbe, the Weser and the North Sea coast. The map shows them from 500 to 700.

From the 200s CE the name was used for sea raiders who struck the coasts of Roman Britain and Gaul, and Rome built forts along the Saxon Shore against them. After Roman rule in Britain ended, many Saxons, with Angles and Jutes, crossed and settled there, becoming the Anglo-Saxons. The kingdoms of Wessex, Essex and Sussex carry their name.

On the continent the Saxons stayed pagan and had no king; local nobles governed, with a yearly assembly. They were the main rivals of the Christian Franks to their south. Charlemagne fought them in the Saxon Wars from 772 to 804. He cut down their holy pillar, the Irminsul, executed many prisoners at Verden in 782 and forced the survivors to be baptised. Their leader Widukind held out for years before accepting baptism in 785.

The Saxons then became one of the main peoples of the Frankish realm. In 919 a Saxon duke, Henry the Fowler, became king of East Francia, and his son Otto I founded the Holy Roman Empire in 962. Their name lives on in Saxony, though that state now lies further south and east.
sum: The Saxons were a Germanic people of northern Germany, between the Elbe, the Weser and the North Sea coast. The map shows them from 500 to 700.
